stem.en: A cell copies its DNA before it divides, not after. Why does this order matter?

text.en: Copying DNA needs far more room than a new small cell has.

feedback.en: Room is not the reason. Follow what each new cell receives.

text.en: The cell must check every copy for errors before it splits.

feedback.en: Checking does not explain the order. Think what each new cell would have.

text.en: Division destroys the DNA that was in the parent cell.

feedback.en: Division shares out the DNA. It does not destroy it.

text.en: With no copy, the new cells could not each get a full set.

feedback.en: Yes. Division only shares out what is already there.

explanation.en: Division shares out what the cell already has. Each daughter cell can have a complete set only if there are two complete sets to share.

hints.en: Imagine dividing with only one set of DNA. What does each new cell get?
